rules.title: Motion respects a reduced-motion preference
rules.description: Where a project animates, it honours the user's declared preference for reduced motion by removing or substantially reducing non-essential movement.
rules.rationale: For users susceptible to motion-triggered disorders, an ignored preference is not an aesthetic disagreement — it is a symptom the interface caused.
rules.remediation: Guard animations behind a reduced-motion query and provide a still equivalent.
rules.$assuranceNote: The detector reports a project that animates with no reduced-motion handling anywhere. Whether each individual animation is correctly guarded is not established by it.

rules.title: Motion serves comprehension rather than decoration
rules.description: Animation explains a relationship, a transition, or a state change, and does not delay the user or interfere with reading and operation.
rules.rationale: Motion is expensive attention. Spent on decoration it costs time on every repetition and buys nothing after the first.
rules.remediation: Keep motion that explains a change and remove motion that only decorates one.
rules.$assuranceNote: Purpose is intent. Duration and easing are visible in source and say nothing about whether the motion earns its place.
